title: Flowchart symbol card
subject: Computing
unit: Spring 1: Think like a computer: algorithms
source: Seeded from computing/y7 lesson 8 (Flowchart symbol card (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 8: Flowcharts and pseudocode. To understand how flowcharts and pseudocode represent the same algorithm

questions.q: Draw a flowchart: input a number, output 'even' or 'odd'.
questions.a: Start; input n; decision: n MOD 2 = 0?; yes: output 'even'; no: output 'odd'; stop.
questions.model: Teacher draws it in diagrams.net, saying the symbol name before each shape.

questions.q: Write the even/odd flowchart as pseudocode.
questions.a: INPUT n; IF n MOD 2 = 0 THEN OUTPUT 'even' ELSE OUTPUT 'odd' ENDIF

questions.q: Core: Draw a flowchart in diagrams.net (or on paper) for a password check: allow 3 tries, then lock. Paste a picture into the portal.
questions.a: Start; tries = 0; loop: input password; decision correct? yes: 'Welcome', stop; no: tries + 1; decision tries = 3? yes: 'Locked', stop; no: back to input.
questions.model: Teacher draws the first three symbols: Start, 'tries = 0', 'INPUT password'.

questions.q: Extend: Write your flowchart as pseudocode.
questions.a: tries = 0; REPEAT INPUT p; tries = tries + 1 UNTIL p = correct OR tries = 3; IF p = correct THEN 'Welcome' ELSE 'Locked'.

questions.q: Stretch: Explain one advantage of a flowchart and one of pseudocode.
questions.a: Flowchart: shows the flow visually for anyone; pseudocode: closer to code, quicker to turn into a program.

questions.q: Start and stop use the... A) diamond B) rounded rectangle C) parallelogram
Big question: give one reason to draw a flowchart before coding.
questions.a: To plan and check the logic and spot mistakes before writing code.
